IncidentCategoryCustomerFriendlyDescript: Following a customers request, we are upgrading underground cables on our electricity network. This will allow for a new connection to the network. Once completed this will improve the reliability of the electricity network in your area and provide the customer with their desired outcome. You may see our engineers prior to the planned power cut carrying out preparation work. To maintain your electricity supply during the work, we'll temporarily connect your property to a generator. There will be brief interruptions to your power while it is connected and removed. If you have solar panels, please switch them off to keep them safely isolated. If your system has an 'island mode' (sometimes called backup or standby mode) you can use that instead. This helps prevent any issues during the power cut. This work is taking place on Brighton Road. Multi way traffic lights will be in place on Brighton Road, Haling Park Road, Junction Road and Drovers Road to allow the work to be carried out safely.

IncidentCategoryCustomerFriendlyDescript: To help keep your electricity supply safe and reliable, we regularly inspect and maintain our equipment. As part of this work, we're removing some overhead cables and placing these underground. We are also removing some over head equipment known as a pole mounted transformer and replacing this with a new ground mounted transformer. This upgrade will help improve the reliability of your electricity supply and reduce the risk of unexpected power cuts in the future as we appreciate your area has been impacted with unplanned power cuts in the last 6 months. To carry out this work safely, we will need to temporarily switch off your electricity, as it is not safe to work on electrical equipment while it is live. We understand that power interruptions are inconvenient, and we will do everything we can to keep disruption to a minimum. This work is taking place off Birch Lane in Flaunden. A road closure will be in place to allow the work to be carried out safely. Access to your property will always be provided.

We need to trim these trees, which requires a temporary power cut because the work cannot be done safely while electricity lines are live. This essential work involves approximately 120 metres of tree cutting across 6 sections of the overhead electricity network. One of our contractors will carry out the work so you may see their vans in the area. This work is taking place in fields along Long Barn Road.

IncidentCategoryCustomerFriendlyDescript: We regularly inspect trees near overhead power lines to keep your electricity supply safe and reliable. A recent inspection found some trees have grown too close to power lines. If unmanaged, branches could touch the overhead lines and cause unexpected interruptions to your electricity supply as we appreciate some customers may have experienced unplanned power cuts in the last 6 months. We need to trim these trees, which requires a temporary power cut because the work cannot be done safely while electricity lines are live. This essential work involves tree cutting across 7 sections of the overhead electricity network. This work is taking place near North End Road.

IncidentCategoryCustomerFriendlyDescript: We regularly inspect electrical equipment in your area to help keep your electricity supply safe and reliable. This work will also reduce the likelihood of unexpected power cuts in the future. To carry out this work safely, we need to temporarily switch off your electricity while we work on the electricity poles. This work is taking place along Hawkesbury Road. Please be aware that there will be a temporary road closure in place to allow the work to be carried out safely. Please expect delays of up to 15 minutes.

Sent by Luke at 08:10 - Thank you for your patience while our engineers worked on the overhead network in the East Grinstead area. We have now restored power to all but one property. We're sorry for any disruption this unexpected power cut caused.

If your power isn't back on, we'd still like to keep you updated. If we aren't currently in contact with you by phone or in person at your property, please call us on 08003163105 which is free from landlines and mobiles.

We know that being without power can be especially difficult, so we're sorry for the outage. Please rest assured our staff will continue to work around the clock to keep the lights on.

Our engineers have arrived on site in the East Grinstead area and are investigating the fault.

You may find your power is going on and off; that is normal for this type of issue and is due to our engineers working to divert power remotely. By doing this, we've managed to restore power to another 13 customers. There are now 16 properties still affected.

We'll keep sending SMS updates until everybody is restored. To stop receiving texts, just follow this link https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP to unsubscribe. Sent by Luke at 07:22.

What will happen next?

This outage is affecting multiple areas, so locations we mention may be further away than you'd expect. We have already sent staff to the area, but at the same time we try to restore power remotely by redirecting the electricity around the faulty section. It's possible your power may go on and off as we try to restore as much power as we can.

The engineer will head to the local substation and after checking the network, will attempt to restore more power from there. If unsuccessful, they will locate and repair the issue, which will take longer to get the lights on.

Our staff work as quickly as they can, so you might not hear about everything we're doing, but we'll always try to give you the clearest information we have.

If you'd like any further information, or if your power is not restored, please call us any time on 08003163105.

We're sorry your power has gone off again.

We believe there may be an underlying issue causing the recent power cuts, but due to the nature of the electricity network, the heat created by a developing fault can cause a break in a cable to reseal itself. This can make it difficult to locate, so while our engineers are testing our equipment thoroughly to pinpoint the issue, this kind of problem may interrupt power multiple times before it's possible for us to fix.

We know that our customers may be worried about the food in the fridge and freezer, so we want to try and help with advice. Food should keep for up to 4 hours in the fridge, and between 24-48 hours in the freezer if you avoid opening them.

Steps.Message:
Sent by David at 13:18 - Our engineers have restored power to all 889 properties in the SG9 0, SG11 2 area, and we're pleased that this is sooner than we estimated. They have diverted power around a faulted piece of overhead network equipment.

We know some properties in the area may have faced other recent interruptions, and we're sorry for the extra disruption. Every outage is fully investigated by our engineers, though power may be lost several times before we can safely find and fix the issue. Our customer services team will keep as many customers updated as possible during these investigations. 

We're sorry for the unplanned disruption. If you need to talk to us, or let us know that your power isn't restored, call us on 08003163105.
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Our engineers have arrived on site in the SG9 0, SG11 2 area to investigate the power cut affecting 292 properties. Specialist engineers are also working to divert power remotely, and this can cause your lights to go on and off. We know that a power cut can be very disruptive, even more so if you are vulnerable. If you're worried about an elderly or ill person in your property who is affected by the power cut today, we are able to provide some support. We'll continue to keep you updated with our engineer's progress but for any concerns or questions, don't hesitate to call us free on 08003163105. For more information on how we support vulnerable customers just click here: https://UKPN.short.gy/PSR
Steps.Name: Customer Service Team

Steps.Message: Sent by David at 12:28 - Our engineers are on their way. We believe the issue is faulty overhead electrical equipment that initially interrupted power to 889 properties. However, we have managed to divert power back to some properties, so 292 properties are still affected. Specialist engineers from our control room will continue to divert power remotely, so your power may come back on at any point. Sometimes we can't restore everyone this way, so we're also sending staff to check our equipment. We're currently estimating power will be on between 14:30-15:30, but this may change depending on what our staff find. Power back on? Sometimes we can't restore everyone this way, so we're also sending staff to check our equipment.

We're currently estimating power will be on between 17:00-18:00, but this may change depending on what our staff find.

Power back on? To stop receiving texts, follow this link https://UKPN.short.gy/STOP to unsubscribe. Otherwise, we'll keep you updated.
